label: Relationship pressure patterns

patterns.label: Performed innocence
patterns.description: A participant presents their purpose or standing as more ordinary, harmless, or detached than the observable sequence supports.

patterns.label: Affinity / recognition entry
patterns.description: Recognition, warmth, similarity, or praise participates in opening access to a later request.

patterns.label: Commitment anchoring
patterns.description: An earlier statement or commitment is used as pressure against reassessment after relevant context changes.

patterns.label: Semantic narrowing
patterns.description: A broader relationship or qualified statement is repeatedly compressed into a smaller wording that carries different practical standing.

patterns.label: Credibility displacement
patterns.description: Attention shifts from the evidence or relationship under question toward whether the evaluator or speaker deserves to be believed.

patterns.label: Investigation inversion
patterns.description: A participant under examination redirects the interaction so the act of examining becomes the primary alleged problem.

patterns.label: Provenance contradiction
patterns.description: A later claim, artifact, or framing conflicts with the source, custody, or sequence that would need to support it.

patterns.label: Status degradation
patterns.description: A participant lowers another participant's status, competence, legitimacy, or relational standing as pressure on judgment.

patterns.label: False-binary pressure
patterns.description: A relationship with more than two truthful possibilities is framed as if only two choices remain.

patterns.label: Authority substitution
patterns.description: Warmth, confidence, identity, institutional status, prior access, or another standing is silently substituted for the authority actually needed.

patterns.label: Record contraction
patterns.description: The usable record is narrowed so qualifiers, corrections, chronology, or inconvenient source relationships disappear from the later framing.

patterns.label: Post-failure narrative inversion
patterns.description: After an effect does not work as intended, the explanation of what happened is rewritten in a way that relocates responsibility or changes the original claim.

boundaries: Observer patterns are descriptive review vocabulary, not instructions for the counterpart model.
Observer patterns are never supplied to Vex as hidden truth or scoring criteria.
A pattern label does not prove motive, manipulation, or moral standing by itself.
Absence of a labeled pattern does not prove an encounter was harmless or well-formed.
Observer classification does not own PASS/FAIL, Memory acceptance, Foundation change, or training.
